cache_continuity.interpretation: Cache depends on stable instructions/agent; switching model within the same agent preserved cache in this test. Do not generalize.

skills.interpretation: Native loading is already lazy: metadata discovery followed by on-demand loading. Do not create a new platform/flag; skill_routing remains OFF.

conclusion: Cache continuity was measured in a real G1/T4 journey through DONE. The skill A/B observed a separate on-demand tool round-trip in one MiMo free sample pair; the prompt delta reflects context resend/cache rather than the ~546-token skill body. No new platform/flag; skill_routing remains OFF. #11 remains PARTIAL despite cache evidence in DONE; #64 remains PARTIAL because there is no skills-assisted completion journey and this A/B is only one pair.
limitations: Token counts are estimates using chars/4, not provider token accounting.
The negative control changes the agent/system prompt, so cacheRead=0 does not isolate other variables.
Skills duplicate names and hybrid-development content divergence are reported risks only; no ownership/content changes were made.
G1/T4 DONE journey busy times are per-session only; no aggregate end-to-end DONE latency is claimed.
Skill A/B has one sample per arm, MiMo free only, and no completion journey with a loaded skill; it is not a causal benchmark.

arm_a.condition: Loaded skill verification-before-completion through the skill tool

skill_load_ab.interpretation: Native lazy loading avoids preloading the 228k-token estimated skill bodies, but loading a skill incurs a separate tool round-trip/inference with context resend. The approximately 34k prompt difference reflects resend/cache behavior, not the skill body size. Do not interpret this one-pair sample as a causal latency or token benchmark.
skill_load_ab.conclusion: No new platform or flag is warranted; skill_routing remains OFF. A skill load is on-demand and costs a round-trip. #64 remains PARTIAL because this is one MiMo free sample per arm and not a skills-assisted completion journey.
limitations: One observation per arm; no statistical inference.
No full completion/DONE journey with a loaded skill was measured.
Reported cost 0 is the observed call cost, not a universal free-cost claim.
Prompt token difference reflects context resend/cache and is not the skill payload size.
